mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates applied to equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship is consistently observed across multiple economic cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 3.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL rising > 0.3 percentage points in three months) signals an increased risk of aggressive monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3pp in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong employment growth (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market that often precedes inflationary pressures and monetary policy tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.2pp in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by GDPC1 growth exceeding 2% and UNRATE below 4.0%), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals a weakening in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when HOUST declines > 0.5% in 1 month during a late-cycle expansion (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that often leads to higher inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO falling > 0.5% in one month) signals an imminent economic slowdown, which typically causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 1 month (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) are strong and housing starts (HOUST) are weak, it indicates a shift in consumer spending away from housing, which may signal an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS growth > 0.5% and HOUST falls > 0.3% in 1 month (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising > 0.5 percentage points in three months), a higher current federal funds rate level is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS is above 4.0% during a tightening cycle (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
